statement: Add deterministic RoadmapManagement and mandatory fresh-task context bootstrap so DevRelay users can capture, evaluate, prioritize, and resume roadmap work from exact approved project state.
objectives: Capture net-new initiatives as auditable candidates without silently mutating approved scope.
Use RequirementsGathering to close initiative intent before keep, defer, merge, or discard disposition.
Maintain an authoritative structured RoadmapBaseline with a concise deterministic Roadmap.md projection.
Load and prove current project, roadmap, lifecycle, Gate, frontier, and blocker context at every fresh DevRelay task.
Keep roadmap authority human-owned and explicit while preserving exact ModuleInvocation inputs.
constraints: RoadmapManagement is cross-cutting and is not inserted as a mandatory software-construction stage.
Fresh-task context applies only to DevRelay tasks in the configured workspace, not unrelated ChatGPT conversations.
Session context never replaces content-addressed ModuleInvocation inputs or becomes hidden Core state.
V1 owns prioritization and disposition, not dates, staffing, scheduling, execution, or work-item status.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh DevRelay task fails closed unless it loads a valid digest-bound SessionContextSnapshot and records a SessionContextReceipt.
A net-new initiative reaches RoadmapGate only after adaptive RequirementsGathering closes at or above 0.99 with no blocking unknowns or contradictions.
RoadmapManagement returns exactly one audited keep, defer, merge, or discard recommendation and never mutates the roadmap directly.
Roadmap.md is a concise deterministic projection of the authoritative RoadmapBaseline.
Every roadmap priority and disposition is reproducible from exact baselines, explicit weights, evidence, and owner approval.
assumptions: The owner's approvals in this task close all twelve RM-001 intake decisions exactly as recorded.
The sealed SIM-001 evidence commit is the immutable implementation baseline for RM-001.
ChatGPT Desktop on Windows remains the release-defining host.
